selectedOriginals.inspection: Selected2015 complete tower original inspected: very tall taper, sparse alternating window faces, rounded red crown merlons, horizontal repair bands, lightning conductors and narrow dark base doorway; surrounding flags/park not part of model.

additionalInspected.inspection: Additional original inspected for entry ambiguity: heavy outward-opening iron door, segmental brick arch, deep thick-wall reveal, slight raised threshold and narrow paved approach/curb beside North Front Street. Temporary2017 tour banner and freestanding yellow sign excluded.

sources.inspection: Maryland Historical Trust primary record read:14storeys,40ft base diameter,20ft top diameter, thick brick shell, low doorway, sparse windows and concrete crenellated parapet.

Aerial inspected: circular flat red roof deck inside approximately16 rounded merlons, western main opening beside North Front Street and narrow own path. South low dark mark conservatively treated as closed aperture, not a second certified entrance. Neighboring pavilion/park sculptures excluded.

scope: Tapering brick shot tower, sparse windows, arched iron entrance, rounded crenellated crown/flat roof deck and own narrow footing. Neighboring buildings, park fixtures and flags excluded.
limitations: Only exterior tower and narrow own footing/entry. Neighboring pavilion/museum and other buildings, park sculptures/fences, temporary signs/banners, flag poles/flags and interiors excluded.
Hidden window positions, exact angular orientation, heights of individual openings and fine brick/parapet details remain estimates.
Independent terrain remains unchanged; geographic readiness requires current visual contact review.

crownDetailReview.inspection: Focused crop of the already inspected2015 original resolves low rounded crown mounds above a continuous parapet, not tall rectangular castle teeth. Brick-facing appearance retained over the parapet structure described as concrete by MHT. Flat roof deck and approximately16 evenly spaced mounds controlled by aerial.
